Write all fractions in lowest terms: Fill in the blanks to make the statements true: [[aside]] Look in any magazine or newspaper and you’re likely to see numbers [[aside]] written as per cents. Listen to any sporting event, and you’ll probably [[aside]] hear statistics reported using per cents. Per cents are everywhere. But [[aside]] what are per cents? The word per cent means for each 100, so a per cent �[[aside]] like 50% is the same amount as the fraction 50 �[[aside]] 100� (or 1 �[[aside]] 2 �) or the decimal [[aside]] 0.50 (or 0.5). Fractions, decimals, and per cents can be used [[aside]] interchangeably to represent parts of a whole quantity. [[aside]] Often, the word percent is used in connection with the per cent of some [[aside]] quantity. For example, you might hear, “Only 3% of voters voted in the [[aside]] last election.” No matter what the quantity, 100% of a quantity always [[aside]] means all of it, and 50% always means half of it. The amount indicated [[aside]] by a certain per cent changes as the size of the quantity changes. For [[aside]] example, 50% of 10 dogs is 5 dogs, but 50% of 100 dogs is 50 dogs.

Kalahari, South Africa 932,400 2. Thar, India 199,430 3. Gibson, Australia 155,400 4. Great Victoria, Australia 647,500 5. Sahara, North Africa 8,598,800 [[aside]] Any number that has an exponent of 0 is equal to 1. [[aside]] So, 2⁰ = 1, 3⁰ = 1, 10⁰ = 1, � [[aside]] 0 �[[aside]] 1� �[[aside]] 2� � � � [[aside]] = 1. [[aside]] For any number a ≠ 0, a⁰ = 1. [[aside]] You can show this by using the division of powers rule. [[aside]] If you start with 1000, and keep dividing by 10, you get this pattern: [[aside]] Any Number Raised to the Power 0 is 1 [[aside]] Now divide by 10 : 10² ÷ 10¹ = 10⁽² ⁻ ¹⁾ = 10¹ [[figure]] [[aside]] 10 = 10¹ [[figure]] �[[aside]] 1 = 10⁰ [[figure]] �[[aside]] Now divide by 10 : 10¹ ÷ 10¹ = 10⁽¹ ⁻ ¹⁾ = 10⁰ [[figure]] [[aside]] When you divide 10 by 10, you have 10¹ ÷ 10¹ = 10⁽¹⁻¹⁾ = 10⁰. [[aside]] You also know that 10 divided by 10 is 1. So you can see that 10⁰ = 1. [[aside]] This pattern works for any base. [[aside]] For instance, 6¹ ÷ 6¹ = 6⁽¹⁻¹⁾ = 6⁰, and 6 divided by 6 is 1. 6⁰ = 1. [[aside]] 1000 = 10³ [[figure]] [[aside]] 100 = 10² [[figure]] [[aside]] Now divide by 10 : 10³ ÷ 10¹ = 10⁽³ ⁻ ¹⁾ = 10² [[figure]] [[aside]] Think and Discuss [[aside]] 1. [[aside]] Scientific notation is a shorthand way of writing such numbers. [[aside]] To express any number in scientific notation, write it as the product of a [[aside]] power of ten and a number greater than or equal to 1 but less than 10. [[aside]] In scientific notation, the number of atoms in a quarter is 9.77 × 10²², and [[aside]] the size of each atom is 3.0 × 10⁻⁸ centimetres across.

items.subject: Science
items.stem: Why is soil erosion relatively less in dense forests as compared to barren, open fields?
items.answer: In dense forests, the tree cover (canopy) prevents rain water from directly falling on the ground/soil. Also roots of the vegetation bind the soil particles and hold them together. As a result soil erosion is minimised. But in barren, open fields the soil is exposed to the falling rain. The soil particles become loose due to the impact of raindrops and the flow of water carries them away. The flowing water further erodes the soil surface aggravating erosion. items.stem: �In a repeater machine with 0 as an exponent, the base machine is applied 0 times. (a) [[figure]] What do these machines do to a piece of chalk? (b) What do you think the value of 6⁰ is? You have seen that a hookup of repeater machines with the same base can be replaced by a single repeater machine. Similarly, when you multiply exponential expressions with the same base, you can replace them with a single expression. Asif Raza thought about how he could rewrite the expression 2²⁰ × 2 . 5 2 ×2 ... it's too long [[figure]] 25 [[figure]] to write out... hmmm... [[figure]] But it's 25 factors of 2 and 5 [[figure]] more. So it's 25 factors of [[figure]] 2, which is 2 . I see... I can [[figure]] just add the exponents! [[figure]] [[aside]] 5 [[figure]] 25 [[figure]] Asif Raza’s idea is one of the product laws of exponents, which can be expressed like this: Multiplying Expressions with the Same Base a^(b) × a^(c) = a^(b+c) Actually, this law can be used with more than two expressions. As long as the bases are the same, to find the product you can add the exponents and use the same base. For example: 3² × 3³ × 3¹⁰ = 3²⁺³⁺¹⁰ = 3¹⁵
items.answer: (a) They do not change its length. (b) 1

[[aside]] Distribution of Primes [[aside]] Remember that a prime number is only divisible by 1 and itself. There are [[aside]] infinitely many prime numbers, but there is no algebraic formula to find [[aside]] them. The largest known prime number, discovered on November 14, 2001, [[aside]] is 2^(13,466,917) –1. In standard form, this number would have 4,053,948 digits. [[aside]] Sieve of Eratosthenes [[aside]] One way to find prime numbers [[figure]] [[aside]] is [[figure]] [[aside]] called [[figure]] [[aside]] the [[figure]] [[aside]] Sieve [[figure]] [[aside]] of [[figure]] [[aside]] Eratosthenes. Use a list of whole [[figure]] [[aside]] numbers in order. Cross off 1. The [[figure]] [[aside]] next number 2 is prime. Circle [[figure]] [[aside]] it. Then cross off all multiples of [[figure]] [[aside]] 2, because they are not prime. [[figure]] [[aside]] Circle the next number on the [[aside]] list. Cross off all of its multiples. Repeat this step until all of the numbers [[aside]] are circled or crossed off. The circled numbers will all be primes. [[aside]] 1. Use the Sieve of Eratosthenes to find all prime number less than 50. [[aside]] 2. On graph paper plot the first 15 prime number. Use the prime number [[aside]] as the x-coordinates and their positions in the sequence as the y-[[aside]] coordinates; 2 is the 1st prime, 3 is the 2nd prime, and so on. [[figure]] [[aside]] 3. options: a × b × c × d [[aside]] Solve [[figure]] [[aside]] • [[aside]] Given y = 2x [[aside]] • [[aside]] Sum of digits at odd places = x + 5 [[aside]] • [[aside]] Sum of digits at even places = 6 + 7 = 13 [[aside]] • [[aside]] Difference = (x + 5) – 13 [[aside]] = x – 8 [[aside]] Now (x – 8) should be equal to 0 or a multiple of 11 (i.e. 11, 22, [[aside]] 33, ..., etc.) [[aside]] x – 8 = 0 [[aside]] x = 8 or x – 8 = 11 [[aside]] x = 11 + 8 = 19 [[aside]] • [[aside]] Since x is a digit so it can take values from 0 – 9 [[aside]] Hence x = 8 [[aside]] Required number is 7568. [[aside]] Revise [[aside]] • [[aside]] 7568 [[aside]] Sum of digits at odd places = 5 + 8 = 13 [[aside]] Sum of digits at even places = 6 + 7 = 13 [[aside]] Difference = 13 – 13 [[aside]] = 0 [[aside]] So Value of x is correct. items.stem: The size of the cells of an organism has no relation with the size of its body. Do you agree? Give reason for your answer.

items.stem: Show diagramatically the electron distributions in a sodium atom and a sodium ion and also give their atomic number.
items.answer: [[figure]] Since the atomic number of sodium atom is 11, it has 11 electrons. A positively charged sodium ion (Na⁺) is formed by the removal of one electron from a sodium atom. So, a sodium ion has 11–1 = 10 electrons in it. Thus, electronic distribution of sodium ion will be 2, 8. The atomic number of an element is equal to the number of protons in its atom. Since, sodium atom and sodium ion contain the same number of protons, therefore, the atomic number of both is 11.

items.subject: Science
items.stem: Describe the structure and function of different types of epithelial tissues. Draw diagram of each type of epithelial tissue.
items.answer: [[aside]] [[aside]] Epithelial tissues are the covering or protective tissues in the animal body. [[aside]] Epithelium covers most organs and cavities within the body and keep [[aside]] different body systems separate. The skin, the lining of the mouth, the [[aside]] lining of blood vessels, lung alveoli and kidney tubules are all made of [[aside]] epithelial tissue. Epithelial tissue cells are tightly packed and form a [[aside]] continuous sheet. They have only a small amount of cementing material [[aside]] between them and almost no intercellular spaces. The permeability of the [[aside]] cells of various epithelia play an important role in regulating the exchange [[aside]] of materials between the body and the external environment and also [[aside]] between different parts of the body. Regardless of the type, all epithelia are [[aside]] usually separated from the underlying tissue by an extracellular fibrous [[aside]] basement membrane. Epithelial tissues are of following types— (1) Simple squamous epithelium (2) Stratified squamous epithelium (3) Columnar epithelium, and (4) Cubodial epithelium. These tissues differ in structure that correlate with their unique functions. For example, in cells lining blood vessels or lung alveoli, where transportation of substances occurs through a selectively permeable surface, there is a simple flat kind of epithelium. This is called the simple squamous epithelium. Simple squamous epithelial cells are extremely thin and flat and form a delicate lining. The skin, oesophagus and the lining of the mouth are also covered with squamous epithelium. Skin epithelial cells are arranged in many layers to prevent wear and tear. Since, they are arranged in a pattern of layers, the epithelium is called stratified squamous epithelium. Where absorption and secretion occur, as in the inner lining of the intestine, tall epithelial cells are present. This columnar epithelium facilitates movement across the epithelial barrier. In the respiratory tract, the columnar epithelial tissue also has cilia, which are hair-like projections on the outer surfaces of epithelial cells. These cilia can move, and their movement pushes the mucus forward to clear it. This type of epithelium is thus ciliated columnar epithelium. Cuboidal epithelium forms the lining of kidney tubules and ducts of salivary glands, where it provides mechanical support. Epithelial cells often acquire additional specialisation as gland cells, which can secrete substances at the epithelial surface. Sometimes a portion of the epithelial tissue folds inward, and a multicellular gland is formed. This is glandular epithelium. [[figure]] (ii) Why is the highest peak in plot A graph slightly delayed? [[figure]] (ii) What is the reason for the different pattern of the two graphs? [[figure]] Fig. 15.1 [[figure]]
items.answer: (i) With addition of chemical fertilizer there is sudden increase in yield due to release of nutrients N,P,K etc in high quantity. The gradual decline in the graph may be due to continuous use and high quantity of chemicals which kills microbes useful for replenishing the organic matter in the soil. This decreases the soil fertility. (ii) Manures supply small quantities of nutrients to the soil slowly as it contains large amounts of organic matter [Hint: importance of organic matter can be included]. It enriches soil with nutrients thereby increasing soil fertility continuously. (iii) The difference in the two graphs indicate that use of manure is beneficial for long duration in cropping as the yield tends to remain high when the quantity of manure increases. In case of Plot B the chemical fertilizers may cause various problems when used continuously for long time. Loss of microbial activity reduces decomposition of organic matter and as a result soil fertility is lost that affects the yield.

items.answer: [[figure]] Gamete represents the sex cell or germ cell in sexual [[figure]] reproduction. There are two types of gametes, male and [[figure]] female. items.subject: Science
items.stem: Why does a magnetic compass needle pointing North and South in the absence of a nearby magnet get deflected when a bar magnet or a current carrying loop is brought near it. Describe some salient features of magnetic lines of field concept.
items.answer: Current carrying loops behave like bar magnets and both have their associated lines of field. This modifies the already existing earth’s magnetic field and a deflection results. Magnetic field has both direction and magnitude. Magnetic field lines emerge from N-pole and enter S-pole. The magnetic field strength is represented diagrammatically by the degree of closeness of the field lines. Field lines cannot cross each other as two values of net field at a single point cannot exist. Only one value, a unique net value, can exist. If in a given [[figure]] region, lines of field are shown to be parallel and equi-[[figure]] spaced, the field is understood to be uniform. [[figure]]
